title: The Biggest Alternating Sum of a Subsequence

concept.title: Two states: the next chosen number will be added, or it will be subtracted
body: Choose some of the numbers of a list, keeping their order (a *subsequence*). The **alternating sum** of the chosen numbers is the first one minus the second plus the third minus the fourth, and so on. Find the largest alternating sum. For `4 2 5 3` the subsequence `4, 2, 5` gives 4 - 2 + 5 = 7, which is the best.

Walk along the list and decide for every number: take it or leave it. What matters about the past is only **how many numbers were taken so far, even or odd**, because that decides the sign of the next one. So keep two values: `ev` is the best alternating sum when an **even** number of values has been taken (the next one will be added; at the start it is 0, the empty choice) and `od` is the best when an **odd** number has been taken (the next one will be subtracted; at the start there is no such choice, so it is "minus infinity"). For a new number `x`: taking it after an even count gives `ev + x` for the odd state, and taking it after an odd count gives `od - x` for the even state; leaving it changes nothing.

body.code:
NEG = -10 ** 18                          # "impossible"
ev, od = 0, NEG
for x in a:
    ev, od = max(ev, od - x), max(od, ev + x)     # both new values use the old ones
print(max(ev, od))

body: The two values are updated **together**: in Python the tuple assignment evaluates the right side first, in C++ and Java use temporary variables. Every number is positive, so the answer ends with the odd state, but taking the maximum of both is the safe way. This is a DP with a state of two numbers; the time is O(n) and the memory O(1). The sum can reach 10^14, so use 64-bit numbers.

statement: A list of `n` positive numbers is given. Choose some of them (at least one), keeping their order, so that the alternating sum (first - second + third - ...) of the chosen numbers is as large as possible. Print that largest alternating sum.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`: the number of values.
hints: Keep two values: the best sum when an even number of values has been taken, and when an odd number has been taken.
A new number x is added after an even count and subtracted after an odd count.
Update both values at the same time, using the old ones.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

# Your code here

explanation: Two values are kept: the best alternating sum with an even number of chosen values (the next one is added) and with an odd number (the next one is subtracted). Each number either extends one of them with the right sign or is left out; the answer is the larger value at the end.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

NEG = -10 ** 18
ev, od = 0, NEG
for x in a:
    ev, od = max(ev, od - x), max(od, ev + x)
print(max(ev, od))
